notices.title: Christmas Day, Friday, Dec 25: meters and street sweeping not enforced
notices.detail: SFMTA does not enforce meters, nightly street sweeping or other parking programs. Recology lists its Christmas Day plan as to be determined.

notices.title: Thanksgiving, Thursday, Nov 26: meters and street sweeping not enforced; trash on the regular schedule
notices.detail: SFMTA does not enforce meters, nightly street sweeping or other parking programs on Thanksgiving Day. On Friday, Nov 27, meters and nightly sweeping are enforced but other programs are not. Recology says drivers service on the regular schedule Thanksgiving Day. The Board of Supervisors does not meet Nov 24.

notices.title: SFMTA taxi customer service window closed Nov 24 to 27
notices.detail: The taxi customer service window is closed Tuesday, Nov 24, through Friday, Nov 27.

notices.title: Public libraries close at 5 pm Nov 25 and are closed Nov 26 and 27
notices.detail: San Francisco Public Library locations close early on Wednesday, Nov 25, and are closed Thanksgiving Day and Friday, Nov 27.
notices.stripLine: Thanksgiving and Friday; early close Wednesday

notices.title: Mayor expands shelter capacity for El Nino storm season
notices.detail: The Mayor's office announced added shelter capacity so people can sleep inside during the storm season. Open the release for locations and how to get a bed.

notices.title: Thanksgiving week: Muni schedules and parking rules
notices.detail: Thanksgiving Day, Thursday, Nov 26: meters, seven-day street sweeping, residential permits, weekday daytime sweeping and commuter towaway are not enforced, and Muni runs a Sunday schedule. Muni runs a weekday non-school schedule Nov 23 to 25 and on Nov 27. On Black Friday, Nov 27, meters, loading zones and nightly street sweeping are enforced. Powell Street closes for Natale from 10 am Friday, Nov 27, to 7 pm Sunday, Nov 29.

source.label: SFMTA transit and traffic advisory, Nov 19

notices.title: Mayor signs legislation expanding legal counsel for renters facing eviction
notices.detail: The Mayor signed legislation expanding legal counsel for renters facing eviction and protecting renters from sudden rent increases.

notices.title: Mayor announces a new Department of Planning and Building
notices.detail: The Mayor's office announced a combined Department of Planning and Building, which it says is meant to build housing and issue permits faster.

notices.title: Muni service to expand after transit funding measures passed
notices.detail: The Mayor's office announced expanded Muni service following the success of the Nov 3 transit funding measures.

notices.title: Mission Branch Library reopens Saturday, Nov 14, at 3359 24th Street
notices.detail: The temporary Mission branch and book drop at 1234 Valencia Street closed at 6 pm on Oct 31. The Mission Branch reopens Nov 14 at 3359 24th Street.

notices.oneLiner: Mission Branch Library reopens Nov 14 at 3359 24th Street

notices.title: Northbound US-101 connector to the Central Freeway fully closed, Friday 11 pm to Monday 6 am (Nov 13 to 16)

notices.stripLine: 101 to Central Freeway shut Fri to Mon

notices.title: Veterans Day, Wednesday, Nov 11: meters enforced, libraries closed, trash pickup as normal
notices.detail: SFMTA enforces parking meters, nightly street sweeping (midnight to 6 am), white zones and safety rules. Not enforced: residential permit time limits, general time limits, weekday daytime street sweeping and unmetered yellow and green zones. Recology collects as normal. All San Francisco Public Library locations are closed. The Board of Supervisors meets as scheduled on Tuesday, Nov 10.

notices.title: Board of Supervisors meets Tuesdays at 2 pm: Nov 10, Nov 17, Dec 1, Dec 8 and Dec 15
notices.detail: No meeting Nov 24 (Thanksgiving week). The Mayor is scheduled to appear Nov 10 and Dec 15 (appearances can be rescheduled; check the agenda). Winter recess runs Dec 16, 2026 through Jan 7, 2027. Meetings air live on SFGovTV Channel 26. Clerk of the Board: (415) 554-5184, board.of.supervisors@sfgov.org.

notices.title: Valkyries victory parade on the Embarcadero today, Wednesday, Nov 4, noon to 2 pm
notices.detail: The parade runs along the Embarcadero from the Ferry Building near Mission Street to Second and King streets; fans can gather from 9 am. The Embarcadero, King Street and nearby blocks (including Market between Drumm and Steuart, and Mission, Howard, Folsom, Harrison and Bryant between Main and the Embarcadero) close in stages from 12:01 am or 8 am until 4 pm. Muni's F and N lines along the Embarcadero are suspended about 9:30 am to 3 pm, with a bus replacing them. BART and Bay Ferry are adding service. The City recommends transit.

notices.title: Election results: updated preliminary counts about 4 pm daily, Nov 4 to 13 (not Nov 11)

posts.gist: Election Day: 501 polling places and the City Hall Voting Center open 7 am to 8 pm; four preliminary results reports after polls close.
Mayor signs legislation strengthening San Francisco's wholesale produce market.
Mayor announces the Nov 4 victory parade for the WNBA champion Golden State Valkyries along the Embarcadero.
Mayor signs legislation expanding the landmark at the site of the Compton's Cafeteria riot.
Mayor signs legislation on renter protections against unwarranted evictions and hidden rental fees.
Mayor signs legislation streamlining the process to build housing.
Mayor declares a local emergency to prepare for El Niño.
Mayor introduces legislation for Freedom West 2.0 in the Western Addition, which could bring nearly 2,400 homes, more than 17% expected to be affordable.
Mayor marks upgrades to three public basketball courts with the Valkyries and Warriors.
Mayor reports an 84% drop in speeding where automated speed cameras operate.

postsNote: Snapshot, not live. These are City releases from sf.gov; most links open the Spanish-language listing of each release because that is the version Agorri could open, and summaries are from the release titles. Social posts from Facebook, Instagram, X and Threads need API access or a collector before they can appear here.

benchmarks.note: FBI figures for 2024, the latest year with matching city, state and national numbers. Rates are offenses reported to police per 100,000 residents (FBI population for San Francisco: 802,856). San Francisco's rates fell from 2023 (violent 710.2, property 5,712.5). The many people who work in or visit San Francisco aren't counted as residents, which pushes per-resident rates up. The FBI advises against ranking places on these numbers alone.
benchmarks.homeNote: FBI, 2024. Per-resident rates; visitors and commuters aren't counted as residents.
benchmarks.fireNote: No fire comparison yet: national fire figures don't match how departments count calls or staff.
